entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nicholas of Osimo was an Italian Franciscan preacher and author, active in the 15th century.


Born in Osimo, Italy, around 1400, Nicholas rose to prominence as a leading voice among the Franciscan Order, advocating for the reform of the Catholic Church and the role of the clergy in society.



His writings, including his most famous work, the 'Summa de Fratris,' showcased his expertise in theology, philosophy, and the social sciences, attracting a wide audience within the Church and beyond.



Despite facing opposition from conservative elements within the Church, Nicholas' ideas contributed significantly to the intellectual and spiritual landscape of the Italian Renaissance.



In 1453, Nicholas of Osimo passed away, leaving behind a legacy as a champion of reform and a voice for the marginalized within the Church.
